text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
All newspapers lead with withdrawal of resignation by Hashim Mohamed Ali, who heads Sukom Ninety Eight Bhd, the company organising the 1998 Commonwealth Games.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad received Lebanon's highest award -- Wisha Al-Akbar (the Grand Cordon of Lebanon) -- from the Lebanese government on Monday night.

-- As the deadly Coxsackie virus claimed its 26th victim on Tuesday, the Health Ministry has made it compulsory for doctors to report not only cases of myocarditis but also any other life-threatening microbial infections.
-- Health Minister Chua Jui Meng ticked off parents for not doing enough to keep their children indoors in view of a viral outbreak which has claimed 26 lives in eastern Sarawak state.
-- Star Publications (M) Bhd expects another year of good profits as newsprint prices have stabilised and its core newspaper business continues to expand.
-- Shrugging off a marginal decline in average profits last year, manufacturing companies are generally upbeat about the year's business outlook, a survey shows.
-- The private sectors of Malaysia and Lebanon have been urged to consider establishing a joint business council to spur cooperation in trade and investments.
-- MBf Capital Bhd will press ahead with plans to add a bank to its stable -- the only "missing link" in establishing a complete supermarket.
